rv.q: This is a terrific piece of work all round, that’s already been showered with Olivier and Critic’s Circle awards.
They each get their moment to shine – and deserve to bask in a by turns lightly enjoyable and powerfully serious-minded summer smash.
There are laughs and there are gasps as John Lithgow's sometimes delightful, sometimes horrible, always compelling Roald Dahl fills the air with his nonsense.
Funny, shocking, thought-provoking, controversial, superbly staged (Nick Hytner) and performed, this play is all that theatre should be.
The play is “subtle, intelligent and stylishly crafted”.

First off there’s John Lithgow (also all the awards) stooping and scowling his way into Dahl, charming in his grandpa-ish grumping at the beginning. He’s a walking metaphor: a giant – of literature, of stature – and big.
Dave Fargnoli thinks Rosenblatt’s writing “could be tighter and more sharply focused”
This is sharply structured and finely honed playwriting at its best

cn.t: Mark Rosenblatt's bold, urgent play about Roald Dahl's antisemitism earns rave reviews, with critics hailing John Lithgow's blistering performance and Nicholas Hytner's immaculate direction of this spectacularly provocative West End transfer.
